find: # The line must follow the branch's last line. When another run published in between,
replace:
last="$PREV_HASH"
            # The line must follow the branch's last line. When another run published in between,
why: when the shell runs, the chain comparison refuses a line that does not follow the branch's last line: a reading built on a branch that has moved since, or a first run's line on a log that holds lines
when the shell runs, a line whose UTC day is before the log's last day file is refused, and nothing is pushed
when the shell runs, the day file is the UTC date of the reading's observed_at, never of the clock when the job runs

find: sha256sum -- "${present[@]}" | cmp -s - SHA256SUMS || fail "a file differs from SHA256SUMS"
replace:
sha256sum -- "${present[@]}" >SHA256SUMS
          sha256sum -- "${present[@]}" | cmp -s - SHA256SUMS || fail "a file differs from SHA256SUMS"
why: when the shell runs, a changed byte in any file of the artifact is refused by the check step, and nothing is pushed
when the shell runs, a reading whose run exited 3 (a reset signal) is published
when the shell runs, a run that exited 1 publishes nothing and the job ends well
when the shell runs, a branch that exists is fetched and the reading laid on top of it
when the shell runs, a reading already in the log adds no commit and leaves a newer latest/ as it is (test/live-workflow.test.ts kills this one too, from the text)
when the shell runs, a fetched branch holding a link, an executable or a submodule is refused and nothing is pushed
